data.title: Google launches Universal Cart for purchases across retailers
data.description:
Google formally opened up shopper access to its new Universal Cart for agentic shopping, laying out artificial intelligence (AI)-powered features for price-tracking and checking ahead of the 2026 holiday shopping season.

Universal Cart, which Google previewed at its I/O developer conference in May, already has support from numerous retailers, including Ulta Beauty, Walmart, Wayfair, some Shopify merchants, and others. In October, Newegg became one of the latest names to integrate Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), which makes online checkout through Google’s Search and Gemini experiences possible.

Ulta Beauty ranks No. 37 in the Top 1000 Database. The database is Digital Commerce 360’s ranking of North America’s leading online retailers by annual web sales. There, Walmart is No. 2, Wayfair is No. 11, and Newegg is No. 86.

In Digital Commerce 360’s and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings, Walmart ranks No. 37, Ulta Beauty No. 123, Wayfair No. 267 and Newegg No. 429. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Which features Google launched with Universal Cart

Google announced online shopper-focused features that would be available at launch with Universal Cart. In the announcement, the company highlighted utility for holiday and discount-tracking scenarios.

“The cart puts you in control, helping to organize your shopping, keep track of items you love from across retailers, stay on top of promos, and enjoy effortless checkout powered by the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP),” wrote Suresh Ganapathy, senior director, product management, consumer shopping at Google, in a corporate blog post dated Oct. 15. “Today, Universal Cart is rolling out in the U.S. across Google Search and in the Gemini app.”

Ganapathy specifically noted that Universal Cart would handle checkout for products from multiple retailers at once, tracking pricing and inventory changes, proposing savings options and enabling purchases from merchants’ own websites when desired.

“Let’s say you save a handbag from Steve Madden to your cart in AI Mode in Search, and later a sweater from Quince and lipgloss from Ulta Beauty in the Gemini app,” Ganapathy explained. “Those products will be there in your cart when you come back later so you can pick up right where you left off.”

Universal Cart use cases for holiday shopping

Ganapathy framed Universal Cart as a means for online shoppers to “stay organized and shop more confidently this holiday season.” He cited “the 60+ billion continually refreshed product listings in Google’s Shopping Graph” as its underlying knowledge set. That data in turn informs responses to shopper prompts.

It then provides checkout options for discovered and selected products for Google Wallet users.

“As the holiday season kicks into high gear, the Universal Cart is just one way we’re giving shoppers the convenience and smarts they need to make the best shopping choices,” he stated.

data.title: Newegg adds Google UCP checkout integration
data.description:
Newegg Commerce Inc. expanded its participation in agentic commerce channels, announcing that it has integrated Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) for online checkout.

The consumer electronics retailer follows other big names, including Wayfair, Walmart, Macy’s and other merchants, that have supported UCP since Google formally launched it in January. The move means that Newegg-sold products will be purchasable within Google’s AI Mode, Google Search and Gemini experiences.

Newegg is No. 86 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool ranks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales and more.

Newegg is also No. 429 in Digital Commerce 360’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Newegg web sales by year

Why Newegg is using Google’s UCP

“AI is changing how the world buys technology, and Newegg intends to be at the forefront of that change,” said Montaque Hou, chief information officer at Newegg. “We moved early to make our catalog shoppable inside AI experiences, and integrating Universal Commerce Protocol powered checkout across Google brings that vision to life in one of the most widely used platforms in the world.”

By integrating UCP, which Google co-developed with retailers and commerce platforms including Etsy, Shopify, Target, Walmart and Wayfair, Newegg remains the merchant of record while providing Google with product catalog data used in AI-powered shopping experiences.

“Wherever someone asks an AI what to buy, we want Newegg ready to answer,” Hou stated.

Newegg’s other recent AI efforts

Use of Google’s UCP follows other AI-related pushes for Newegg over the past year. Those have included Celeste, the company’s own conversational AI assistant on the Newegg website, as well as support for listings displayed in Perplexity’s AI-enabled search experience.

Now, it hopes to speed up the shopping process for Google users. Online shoppers using Google’s supported platforms will be able to use Google Pay for Newegg purchases. Moreover, they will be able to do so without leaving their search results or prompts when they decide to buy.

“Newegg enabling UCP-powered checkout on Google marks a new milestone as we scale agentic commerce,” said Ashish Gupta, vice president and general manager for merchant shopping at Google. “We’re building the future of AI-driven shopping together as an industry and this is another strong example of businesses delivering delightful, diverse experiences and products for their shoppers.”

data.title: Edible Brands drives engagement through refresh of loyalty program, app
data.description:
Edible Brands relaunched its mobile app and loyalty program in late April, and the retailer has since seen meaningful results, according to chief digital officer Erica Randerson.

The retailer redesigned its mobile app, which is available on iOS and Android, to “make gifting easier and more intuitive from discovery to checkout,” according to its announcement. Its new loyalty program features four membership tiers. Existing members’ points and rewards automatically transferred to the new experience.

Edible Brands chose to do the relaunch to address digital experience, improve customer experience opportunities and unlock new features. The app now includes features such as birthday reminders and curation of gift lists that users can share.

“As you go into the Edible app today, you’re going to be introduced to a lot more products than you would necessarily even on our mobile website or our desktop website,” Randerson told Digital Commerce 360. “We’re really marketplace forward.”

The app now includes both Edible franchise-fulfilled products as well as those from partners, she noted.

Edible Brands is No. 182 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

Edible Brands is also No. 581 in Digital Commerce 360’s new AI Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Consumer engagement with new Edible Brands app and loyalty program

Since the relaunch, Edible Brands’ mobile app traffic has increased 200%, Randerson shared. It’s also converting at more than 3%.

Edible Brands’ app has 160,000 downloads since the relaunch through the end of August. Additionally, consumers have created 25,000 new accounts.

More than a third (34%) of Edible Brands’ customers who had transacted with the retailer digitally since January 2024 have returned to shop through the mobile app since the relaunch, she added.

“We’ve seen a lot of movement of existing customers that were not app customers convert into app customers, which is also exactly what we were hoping for,” Randerson said. “We’re considering it a success so far and are excited to see both the loyalty platform and the overall app experience continue to evolve.”

So far in 2026, 66% of Edible Brands’ website revenue comes from its mobile site visitors. The remaining 34% comes from its desktop site visitors.

But in terms of overall revenue, desktop represents 36% of revenue, while its mobile website represents 59%. Edible Brands’ mobile app users generate 5% of the retailer’s revenue.

And although Edible Brands’ average order value (AOV) is similar across all three, it’s highest on desktop. By channel, its AOV is:

  • $89 on desktop
  • $83 on mobile website
  • $82 on mobile app

Edible Tests gift recipient campaign

Edible Brands said it launched a campaign in late Q1 2025 aimed at capturing gift recipient customer email addresses. Its goal was to reach them for promotional marketing and ultimately convert those recipients to customers.

Gift recipients all receive a hang tag with a QR code that leads to a landing page. There, the retailer asks for contact information in exchange for a free Dipper Fruit Cone at any local store, plus a promo code for online orders.

Since launch, Edible Brands has captured more than 175,000 new contacts, Randerson shared. Nearly 10% of those recipients visited an Edible store to redeem their free gift. That has driven incremental revenue for the system with an AOV around $62. Randerson noted that the AOV of this recipient-turned-customer is about $10 lower than the overall customer average.

data.title: Commerce.com and eBay avoid September declines in Ecommerce Stock Index results
data.description:
New results are in from September activity in the Baird/Digital Commerce 360 Ecommerce Stock Index. All four categories tracked by the index fell during the month, as the overall index underperformed the S&P 500.

Still, seven companies’ share prices went positive for the month, with Commerce.com, Xometry, Wayfair and eBay among them.

September takeaways from the Baird/Digital Commerce 360 Ecommerce Stock Index

  • The Baird/Digital Commerce 360 Ecommerce Stock Index fell 8.1% in September, with each category that it tracks ending the month negative.
  • September index leaders included Commerce.com (+31%), Xometry (+11%) and Global-E (+6%).
  • Wayfair (+3%) and eBay (+2%) also saw gains in an otherwise difficult month for technology stocks and a flat S&P 500.

This index is a collaboration between Digital Commerce 360 and the financial advisory, capital markets, asset management and private equity firm Baird. It intends to provide perspective into how public markets value companies and technology providers that power digital commerce. The index contains four categories capturing activity extending throughout the Americas and China:

  1. Online Marketplaces
  2. Online Retail
  3. Ecommerce Technology
  4. International Companies

Readers should note that this index complements insights from Digital Commerce 360’s Top 2000 Database. The market research tool specifically tracks North American online retailers and their web sales.

The Baird/Digital Commerce 360 Ecommerce Stock Index, meanwhile, covers both B2C retail and B2B ecommerce companies, in addition to the technology vendors that serve them, with a broader focus on global activity. All commentary and reporting is provided for informational purposes only and is not intended to be financial advice.

Click here to read August’s ecommerce stock index results.

September ecommerce stock index results

“The Baird/Digital Commerce 360 Ecommerce Stock Index in September retraced recent monthly gains, declining 8.1% from August and underperforming the S&P, which was 0.5% lower for the month,” said Colin Sebastian, Baird’s managing director and senior research analyst covering internet/ecommerce.

As with previous swings in share prices over the past year, September’s downward pressure accompanied new developments in AI as markets reacted to agentic features, where technology companies pitched use cases for their latest models, apps and features.

“We believe the bulk of the pressure on Ecommerce stocks was due to increasing investor concerns over the impact of agentic commerce on legacy companies, as personal assistants such as Muse (Meta) and Instinct showed off their shopping and travel booking capabilities,” Sebastian noted. “As such, Online Retail and Marketplaces subsectors were hit hardest in September, down 14% and 9%, respectively, while Ecommerce Technology stocks were flat, as some of those platforms may even benefit from agents shopping on behalf of users.”

Nevertheless, some of September’s strongest performances came out of the Marketplaces and Technology sectors.

Top-performing ecommerce stocks in September

Leading the index in September, ecommerce platform Commerce.com (formerly BigCommerce) reversed its decline from August. The company’s share price finished September 31% higher than its August close as investors grew more confident in the company’s potential to benefit from ecommerce activity following cost reductions.

Next, digital manufacturing services company Xometry followed, up 11% from its August finish. The cross-border ecommerce platform Global-E was up 6%.

Meanwhile, Wayfair (+3%) and eBay (2%) also went positive for the month. Growth for eBay came in the aftermath of the online marketplace’s fiscal Q2 earnings results in August. The report showed that eBay gross merchandise volume (GMV) rose 26% year over year.

“Conversely, weakest performers during the month included online retailers 1-800-Flowers (-32%), Bed, Bath & Beyond (former Overstock business), which was down another 25%, and Chewy (-24%),” Sebastian stated. “Nonetheless, our checks still suggest ongoing healthy ecommerce trends across North America, and we expect solid Q4 ‘Holiday period’ online spending with potential upside to our initial 6% year-over-year industry growth forecast for 2026.”

data.title: Walmart opens automation-infused fulfillment center in California
data.description:
Walmart announced the opening of its fifth next-generation fulfillment center in Stockton, California. The facility, spread across 900,000 square feet, will increase Walmart’s storage capacity and allow it to fulfill more orders across California and the West Coast, according to the retailer.

Walmart ranks No. 2 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 1000 Database, which tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales.

Walmart is also No. 37 in Digital Commerce 360’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

What distinguishes Walmart’s new fulfillment center in Stockton

The centerpiece of Walmart’s Stockton fulfillment center is its automated, high-density storage and retrieval system that brings products directly to associates rather than requiring workers to travel the facility floor. That reduces an otherwise 12-step fulfilment process to just five steps, leaving more time for workers to focus on higher-value tasks, Walmart said.

Walmart now processes more than half of its ecommerce fulfillment volume through automated facilities, according to figures the company shared with investors along with Walmart online sales updates in its fiscal Q2 earnings results. 3,100 of Walmart’s U.S. stores also use automated freight to some capacity. 

Combined with Walmart’s broader fulfillment network, the company says its next-generation fulfillment centers now enable it to reach 95% of the U.S. population with next- or two-day shipping.

“We’re bringing together associates with advanced technology and automation to create a safer, more efficient operation that can fulfill more orders and get products to customers faster,” said Karisa Sprague, senior vice president in fulfillment operations at Walmart U.S. in a written statement. “This facility is an important investment in the Central Valley and a critical part of how we’re building the next generation of Walmart’s fulfillment network across the West Coast.”

Fast delivery’s importance for Walmart

Delivery speed has been central to Walmart’s ecommerce plan in recent quarters.

Walmart U.S. online sales grew 26% in Q1, with delivery speed cited as “a key catalyst for growth around the world” by Rainey. Walmart can now reach about 60% of the U.S. population through delivery in 30 minutes or less, a capability it has expanded to 38 U.S. markets.

Meanwhile, store-fulfilled delivery has more than doubled over the past two years, with more than 36% of those orders delivered in under three hours. 

“Speed matters, and we have a significant competitive advantage,” Walmart CEO and president John Furner told investors in August.

How Walmart Fulfillment Services will use the center

Importantly, the Stockton facility is not only for Walmart’s first-party ecommerce business. 

Walmart Fulfillment Services (WFS), the company’s end-to-end third-party fulfillment offering for marketplace sellers, will also use the space to fulfill orders for merchants selling on Walmart.com. That makes the opening directly relevant for the growing base of brands and distributors selling through the Walmart Marketplace.

Units shipped same day or next day through WFS grew nearly 150% in fiscal Q1, according to John David Rainey, chief financial officer at Walmart.
